newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates stable, strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates stable, strong demand.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were stable despite a money shortage that left some demand uncovered, dealers said.
"Today, we have exhausted the entire supply and banks even started withdrawing funds that were previously placed," one dealer said.

"Friday is normally difficult because of the due payments and many had to lay money for monthly pensions," she said, adding that a total of 35 million kuna were withdrawn from previous interbank borrowings.
Fresh morning deals totalled 29.3 million kuna, leaving a shortage of 12 million kuna.
Call money rates, which accounted for most of the trade, were steady at 10.5 percent. One smaller one-month deal was struck at 15 percent, while one-week money went at 12 percent.
Overnight trade totalled 47.7 millon kuna, mostly borrowed by two banks to maintain their mandatory reserves.
